You knew you shouldn't touch anything, but like any protagonist in a horror story, your curiosity got the best of you and now you've accidentally awoken an evil presence in the house. You'll have to undo the curse to escape with your sanity or forever be haunted! It's a fast, easy-to-learn game that uses push your luck set destruction. Decide how risky to play as you venture deep into the haunted house. Do you take first choice of the items and risk attracting haunts, or play it safe? Collect the right items and you can dispel some of your curses. Number of players: 2 - 5 Game duration: 22 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Don't Go In There and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Reveal a New Room 4 Game end 4.1 1. Trigger Cursed Cards with Game End Effects 4.2 2. Ghosts 4.3 3. Winner 5 Cursed cards 5.1 Amulet 5.2 Cat 5.3 Clocks 5.4 Doll 5.5 Holy Water 5.6 Mask 5.7 Mirror 5.8 Music Box 5.9 Portrait 5.10 Ring 5.11 Tome 5.12 Twin 6 Rooms 6.1 Attic 6.2 Basement 6.3 Hallway 6.4 Library 6.5 Nursery 6.6 Secret Passage Overview The player with the FEWEST Curses win. During the game, you will acquire Cursed cards that will have a Curse value. Try to collect cards with fewer Curses on them and dispel cards with lots of curses. When you dispel a a card it flips over and its Curses no longer add to your total. Sometimes you'll get haunted by Ghosts. Having a few ghost tokens is okay. But if you end with the MOST ghosts you will gain a lot of Curses. Flashlights protect you from Ghosts. It's risky going further into the haunted house, but you can get 1st choice of the cards. Setup There are multiple Cursed card types but not all will be used each game. At the beginning of the game, several Cursed card types will be selected (5/6/7/8 different types for 2/3/4/5 players). Cards are then shuffled and some are randomly removed (16/12/8/4 removed cards for 2/3/4/5 players). Gameplay On your turn you must place one of your Meeples into a Room. If it is the 3rd Meeple in the Room then the Room will be resolved. Placing a Meeple Place 1 Meeple from your supply on an unoccupied space in any Room. Each placed Meeple will allow to claim one of the cards above the Room. A Meeple placed further up has a better chance of getting 1st choice of cards, but an increased chance of taking Ghosts tokens. Some Rooms have an effect that will activate immediately after placing a Meeple into them. If you place the 3rd Meeple the Room is immediately resolved. Otherwise play passes to the next player. Resolving a Room 1. Roll for Ghosts Roll a number dice equal to the total of the dice symbols on all cards above the Room board. The owner of each Meeple takes Ghosts tokens equal to the number of Ghosts rolled minus the number of Flashlights on the Meeple's space. 2. Take Cursed Cards Beginning with the Meeple in the highest space in the room and continuing down, the owner of the Meeple must take a Cursed card of their choice and adds it to a face-up tableau. Some cards will trigger an effect immediately after claiming them. 3. Reveal a New Room Once all Meeples have claimed cards, the Room is flipped to its opposite side and 3 new cards are dealt to the Room. If no cards remain in the deck, the Room board is removed from the game. Play continues with the next player after the player whose Meeple triggered Room resolution. Once every card has been claimed and all 3 Rooms have been removed from play the game ends. Game end The game ends when all Cursed cards have been taken. Once game end is triggered, the following steps are resolved. 1. Trigger Cursed Cards with Game End Effects All players trigger the end game effects of all end game Cursed cards visible in their tableau. 2. Ghosts Reveal the Ghost tokens of all players. [Rating: 2/10] I don’t like this game especially if only two of you are playing. It’s highly likely that twins won’t resolve because you don’t know if you’ll be shuffling the complete set of twins in your 2-player deck. And to make matters worse, ghosts only count if you’ve got the most number of ghosts. So if during the game you already have plenty of ghosts, you no longer have a chance to win. Additionally, you can’t eliminate your ghosts if it’s a 2-player game. This game sucks!

[Rating: 2.5/10] complicated rules for a simple game, even when you win you feel like you've lost, unsatisfying

[Rating: 3/10] After Crypt, Canvas and now Don't Go In there, I can simply conclude that R2i can not make a good game despite how many gimmicks they brought into the packaging

[Rating: 3/10] [b]1st Play Thoughts [bgcolor=#FF6699][color=#FF6699]-[/color] [b]3[/b] [color=#FF6699]-[/color][/bgcolor] (Oct 2023):[/b]  I played this digitally on Board Game Arena and did not care for the game at all. It essentially boils down to collecting a bunch of cards you don't want and trying to get the lowest score possible. It didn't really seem to matter what card you got, they were all quite similar and the game seemed fairly random. The artwork was interesting, I sort of liked it but didn't really like it at the same time. The Halloween theme is fun and the game seems to have some pop culture 

[Rating: 3.5/10] Plays pretty awful at 2 player, so yet another game they added the 2 to the box to sucker people in. Can see this being a fine set collection style game for light gamers at higher player counts around Halloween though.  2 player this is a straight - 0 4+ players - 7

[Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  Set collection with ghosts and worker placement of a sort. It was fine but nothing I need to acquire nor play again.

[Rating: 4/10] There are some reasonable ideas here but the game is very underdeveloped and so has lots of issues, e.g. the fact that nothing scales with the number of players. I might go as high as 5 except for the terrible graphic design; I understand they wanted atmosphere but having that at the expense of not being able to read the cards is unacceptable.

[Rating: 4/10] I thought the not wanting to get cards plus the atypical way you draft cards could be interesting, but this game was pretty mediocre for me. Somehow despite what seems like should work on paper didn't lead to a game that felt particularly tense.

[Rating: 4/10] Artwork was not my type when first started playing. However, quite simple game for what it is and some small element of luck. However, you can count and block and hence seems quite fun. Played on BGA. Would play more if theme and artwork was more my style!
